# Sources behind the rules

<!-- Generated by packages/cli/scripts/sources-doc.mjs from packages/cli/src/rules/sources.json. Edit the JSON, then re-run the script. -->

Every ContextScope rule carries a *why it matters*. This page lists what that rationale rests on, and says plainly where it rests on nothing but our judgement.

- **sourced**: a cited source documents the mechanism the rule relies on.
- **inferred**: the mechanism follows from cited sources, but no source states the rule itself.
- **opinion**: a product judgement. Every numeric threshold (8k tokens, 4k handoff, 6k startup budget) is an opinion unless a source gives the number.

52 sources · rules: 21 sourced, 14 inferred, 1 opinion · generated 2026-09-29

Precision on real repositories is measured separately, in [evaluation-findings.md](evaluation-findings.md).

Cognition's advice is to share context, not forbid the read. *Caveat:* Claude Code forks inherit the parent context and cache, which is the documented alternative. |

## Sources

### Vendor documentation

<a id="cc-best-practices"></a>
- **[Best practices for Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices)**: Anthropic (Claude Code docs), 2026
  Official Claude Code guidance built around the constraint that the context window fills fast and performance degrades as it fills.
  - CLAUDE.md loads every session; keep it concise and prune it — "Bloated CLAUDE.md files cause Claude to ignore your actual instructions!"
  - Exclude things Claude can infer from code, file-by-file descriptions, and frequently changing information.
  - Use /clear between unrelated tasks; a clean session with a better prompt usually beats a long corrected one.
  - Use subagents so broad investigation does not consume the main context; hooks are deterministic while CLAUDE.md is advisory.
  - Used by: B-03, B-08, B-13, S-01, S-07
<a id="cc-memory"></a>
- **[How Claude remembers your project (CLAUDE.md, rules, auto memory)](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory)**: Anthropic (Claude Code docs), 2026
  Reference for CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md loading, path-scoped rules, auto memory and instruction troubleshooting.
  - Target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md; longer files consume more context and reduce adherence; imports still load at launch.
  - Rules with `paths` frontmatter load only when Claude reads matching files.
  - "if two rules contradict each other, Claude may pick one arbitrarily"; audits flag references to files that don't exist and outdated instructions.
  - Auto memory loads the first 200 lines / 25KB of MEMORY.md each session; CLAUDE.md is delivered as a user message and is not enforced.
  - Used by: B-02, B-06, B-10, B-16, H-01, H-02, H-05, H-07, S-01, S-02, S-05, S-06, S-07, S-10
<a id="cc-costs"></a>
- **[Manage costs effectively](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/costs)**: Anthropic (Claude Code docs), 2026
  Explains where Claude Code token spend comes from and concrete ways to reduce it.
  - Each request re-sends the full conversation, so a one-line question in a long session still pays for the whole history (at cached rates).
  - MCP tool definitions are deferred by default; still, disable unused servers and prefer CLI tools.
  - Hooks can preprocess output (e.g. grep a log) and skills can replace exploratory file reads; move specialised CLAUDE.md content to skills.
  - Delegate verbose operations to subagents; agent teams use roughly 7x the tokens of a standard session.
  - Used by: B-02, B-09, B-10, B-11, B-13, B-15, H-01, H-02, H-04, H-06, H-07, S-01, S-06, S-09, S-11
<a id="cc-subagents"></a>
- **[Create custom subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents)**: Anthropic (Claude Code docs), 2026
  Documents subagents as isolated context windows that return results to the main conversation.
  - Each subagent has its own context window, system prompt, tools and permissions.
  - Intended for side tasks that would flood the main conversation; returns only the summary.
  - Many subagents returning detailed results can consume significant main context.
  - The description field decides delegation.
  - Used by: B-05, H-03
<a id="cc-hooks"></a>
- **[Hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks)**: Anthropic (Claude Code docs), 2026
  Reference for hook events, inputs and how hook output reaches the model.
  - SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit plain-text stdout is added to Claude's context.
  - additionalContext, systemMessage and plain stdout are capped at 10,000 characters.
  - Over the cap, output is saved to a file and replaced by a path plus a preview of up to 2,000 characters.
  - Used by: B-16, S-11
<a id="cc-context-window"></a>
- **[Explore the context window](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/context-window)**: Anthropic (Claude Code docs), 2026
  Interactive walkthrough of what fills Claude Code's context at startup and during a session, and what survives compaction.
  - System prompt, CLAUDE.md, memory, skill listing and MCP tool names all load before the first prompt; MCP schemas stay deferred by default.
  - For PostToolUse hooks, plain stdout on exit 0 goes to the debug log, not the context; additionalContext does enter.
  - After compaction, root CLAUDE.md and memory are re-injected; path-scoped rules and hook-added context are summarised away; up to five recent files are re-read.
  - Subagent file reads never touch the parent's window; only the summary returns.
  - Used by: B-05, B-07, B-10, H-04, S-11
<a id="cc-prompt-caching"></a>
- **[How Claude Code uses prompt caching](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/prompt-caching)**: Anthropic (Claude Code docs), 2026
  Explains Claude Code's prefix-cache layout and which user actions invalidate it.
  - Every message re-sends the full context; the cache matches an exact prefix, so an early change recomputes everything after it.
  - Invalidators: model switch, effort change (most models), fast mode, MCP/plugin changes when tools load upfront, compaction, image eviction, upgrades.
  - Editing CLAUDE.md mid-session neither invalidates the cache nor applies until /clear, /compact or restart.
  - A subagent's first request does not read the parent's cache; a fork does.
  - Used by: B-04, B-06, B-09, B-11, B-16, H-05
<a id="cc-skills"></a>
- **[Extend Claude with skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills)**: Anthropic (Claude Code docs), 2026
  Reference for SKILL.md format, frontmatter, the skill listing budget and troubleshooting.
  - The description is what Claude uses to decide when to load a skill; if omitted, the first non-empty body line is used.
  - Combined description + when_to_use is truncated at 1,536 characters; the whole listing has a budget of ~1% of the window and drops descriptions of least-used skills on overflow.
  - Malformed frontmatter YAML: the skill loads with empty metadata, so /skill-name works but Claude cannot match on description.
  - Every listed skill adds to context on every turn whether or not it is used.
  - Used by: S-03, S-04
<a id="cc-mcp"></a>
- **[Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp)**: Anthropic (Claude Code docs), 2026
  MCP configuration in Claude Code, including tool search (deferred definitions) and output limits.
  - Tool search is the default: tool names are listed, full schemas load on demand.
  - Tool search is unavailable with a custom ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, when disabled, or on some older models; then all definitions load upfront.
  - Warns when an MCP output exceeds 10,000 tokens; default maximum 25,000 tokens, with oversize results saved to a file.
  - Used by: B-01, H-06, S-09
<a id="cc-sessions"></a>
- **[Manage sessions](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sessions)**: Anthropic (Claude Code docs), 2026
  How resume, continue, branch and transcripts work in Claude Code.
  - A resumed session restores full history including tool calls and results.
  - For large idle sessions (>100k tokens, ~1h), Claude Code offers resume-from-summary because the cache has expired and full history would be reprocessed.
  - Summaries cost less per request but whatever they omit leaves Claude's context.
  - Used by: B-16
<a id="cc-tools-reference"></a>
- **[Tools reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/tools-reference)**: Anthropic (Claude Code docs), 2026
  Per-tool behaviour of Claude Code's built-in tools, including built-in output caps.
  - A whole-file Read past the token limit returns a first page with a PARTIAL view notice and offset/limit guidance.
  - Glob results are capped at 100 files with a truncation flag; Grep supports head_limit.
  - Bash output is inline up to roughly 30,000 characters by default, then a file path plus preview.
  - Used by: B-01, B-03, B-14
<a id="claude-prompt-caching-api"></a>
- **[Prompt caching (Claude API)](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching)**: Anthropic (Claude Platform docs), 2026
  API reference for prefix caching, its pricing and invalidation hierarchy.
  - Cache writes cost 1.25x base input (5-minute TTL) or 2x (1-hour); reads cost 0.1x (lower on some newer models).
  - Prefix order is tools, then system, then messages; changing tool definitions invalidates everything after.
  - Prompts below a model-specific minimum (512-4,096 tokens) cannot be cached.
  - Used by: B-09, S-08
<a id="claude-context-windows-api"></a>
- **[Context windows (Claude API)](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-windows)**: Anthropic (Claude Platform docs), 2026
  Explains what counts toward the context window and why more context is not automatically better.
  - "more context isn't automatically better"; accuracy and recall degrade as tokens grow (context rot).
  - System prompt, all messages including tool results, and tool definitions all count toward the window.
  - Cached prefixes still occupy the window: caching changes price, not size.
  - Used by: B-04, B-08, B-17
<a id="claude-context-editing"></a>
- **[Context editing (Claude API)](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/context-editing)**: Anthropic (Claude Platform docs), 2026
  API feature that clears old tool results (and optionally tool inputs) as a conversation grows.
  - Older tool results such as file contents or search results are no longer needed once processed.
  - Clearing replaces results with placeholders, oldest first; tool call inputs can be cleared too.
  - Clearing invalidates cached prefixes, so clear enough tokens at once to be worth it.
  - Used by: B-01, B-12, B-17
<a id="claude-compaction-api"></a>
- **[Compaction overview (Claude API)](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/compaction)**: Anthropic (Claude Platform docs), 2026
  Server-side summarisation of older turns to keep long conversations inside the window.
  - Compaction keeps active context small because response quality degrades as a conversation grows.
  - Offers a custom summarisation prompt for when the default summary drops something a later turn needs.
  - Recent turns can be kept verbatim while older ones are summarised.
  - Used by: B-07
<a id="claude-token-counting"></a>
- **[Token counting (Claude API)](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/token-counting)**: Anthropic (Claude Platform docs), 2026
  Free endpoint to count input tokens (system, tools, messages) before sending a request.
  - Counts are estimates and may differ slightly from billed input.
  - Claude Opus 4.7+ tokenizer yields roughly 30% more tokens for the same text than earlier models.
  - Recount per target model rather than reusing counts.
  - Used by: H-05
<a id="codex-agents-md"></a>
- **[Custom instructions with AGENTS.md (Codex)](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/agent-configuration/agents-md)**: OpenAI, 2026
  How Codex discovers and concatenates AGENTS.md files.
  - Global then project files are concatenated root-down; closer files appear later and take precedence.
  - project_doc_max_bytes defaults to 32 KiB; Codex stops adding files once the combined size hits it.
  - Empty files are skipped.
  - Used by: S-01, S-12
<a id="codex-config-reference"></a>
- **[Codex configuration reference](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference)**: OpenAI, 2026
  Reference for Codex config.toml keys, including context-related limits.
  - tool_output_token_limit budgets how much of each tool output is stored in history.
  - model_auto_compact_token_limit sets the compaction trigger.
  - MCP servers support enabled_tools / disabled_tools lists.
  - Used by: B-01
<a id="codex-mcp"></a>
- **[Model Context Protocol in Codex](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp?surface=cli)**: OpenAI, 2026
  Configuring MCP servers in Codex, including per-server tool filtering and output budgets.
  - Per-server allowlist (enabled_tools) and denylist (disabled_tools).
  - Per-tool output token budget to limit how much context a response consumes.
  - Used by: H-06, S-08, S-09
<a id="openai-prompt-caching"></a>
- **[Prompt caching (OpenAI API)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching)**: OpenAI, 2026
  OpenAI's automatic exact-prefix prompt caching for prompts of 1,024+ tokens.
  - Requires an exact prefix match; put static instructions first and dynamic content last.
  - Cached reads are billed at a fraction of uncached input and reduce latency.
  - Used by: B-09
<a id="gemini-cli-gemini-md"></a>
- **[Provide context with GEMINI.md files](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/gemini-md/)**: Google (Gemini CLI docs), 2026
  How Gemini CLI loads hierarchical GEMINI.md context files.
  - Context files are concatenated and sent "to the model with every prompt".
  - Global, workspace and just-in-time files; /memory show displays the concatenation.
  - Used by: S-01

### Standards

<a id="agent-skills-spec"></a>
- **[Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification)**: agentskills.io, 2026
  Open format spec for SKILL.md directories and frontmatter.
  - name (1-64 chars, lowercase/digits/hyphens, matches directory) and description (1-1024 chars, non-empty) are required.
  - Description should say what the skill does and when to use it, with task keywords.
  - Metadata ~100 tokens at startup; SKILL.md body recommended under 5,000 tokens / 500 lines.
  - Used by: S-03, S-04
<a id="agents-md-standard"></a>
- **[AGENTS.md](https://agents.md/)**: Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation), 2026
  The open AGENTS.md format for giving coding agents project instructions.
  - A predictable place for build, test and style instructions for agents.
  - Nested files in monorepos; the closest file takes precedence.
  - Treat it as living documentation kept current with the project.
  - Used by: S-07, S-12
<a id="mcp-spec-tools"></a>
- **[Model Context Protocol specification: Tools (2025-06-18)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/server/tools)**: Model Context Protocol, 2025
  Defines how MCP servers list and describe tools to clients.
  - Each tool carries a name, description and JSON Schema inputSchema (optional outputSchema) returned by tools/list.
  - Servers can notify clients when the tool list changes (listChanged).
  - Used by: S-08

### Engineering posts

<a id="anthropic-context-engineering"></a>
- **[Effective context engineering for AI agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents)**: Anthropic, Prithvi Rajasekaran, Ethan Dixon, Carly Ryan, Jeremy Hadfield, 2025
  Frames context as a finite attention budget and lays out curation techniques for long-running agents.
  - Recall from context declines as token count grows (context rot); aim for the smallest set of high-signal tokens.
  - Clearing old tool results is described as the lightest-touch form of compaction.
  - Compaction risks dropping details whose importance only shows up later.
  - Sub-agents should return a condensed summary, often 1,000-2,000 tokens; external notes files carry state across resets.
  - Used by: B-01, B-04, B-05, B-07, B-10, B-12, B-13, S-10
<a id="anthropic-writing-tools"></a>
- **[Writing effective tools for agents — with agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents)**: Anthropic, Ken Aizawa et al., 2025
  Guidance on designing agent tools, with a section on keeping tool responses token-efficient.
  - "we restrict tool responses to 25,000 tokens by default" in Claude Code.
  - Recommends pagination, range selection, filtering and truncation with sensible defaults.
  - A concise response mode used about a third of the tokens of the detailed mode.
  - Too many or overlapping tools distract agents from efficient strategies.
  - Used by: B-01, B-02, B-03, B-14, H-01, S-08
<a id="anthropic-multi-agent-research"></a>
- **[How we built our multi-agent research system](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/multi-agent-research-system)**: Anthropic, Jeremy Hadfield, Barry Zhang, Kenneth Lien, Florian Scholz, Jeremy Fox, Daniel Ford, 2025
  Lessons from Anthropic's orchestrator/sub-agent research system, including cost and coordination failures.
  - Subagents compress: each explores in its own window and returns the most important tokens.
  - Agents use ~4x the tokens of chat; multi-agent systems ~15x.
  - "without detailed task descriptions, agents duplicate work, leave gaps".
  - Subagents can write outputs to external storage and pass lightweight references back to cut copying overhead.
  - Used by: B-05, B-06, B-15, H-03
<a id="anthropic-building-effective-agents"></a>
- **[Building effective agents](https://www.anthropic.com/research/building-effective-agents)**: Anthropic, Erik Schluntz, Barry Zhang, 2024
  Argues for simple, composable agent designs and careful agent-computer interface (tool) design.
  - Agentic systems trade latency and cost for task performance; add complexity only when it pays.
  - Tool definitions deserve as much prompt-engineering care as the main prompt.
  - Choose tool formats that avoid needless overhead for the model.
  - Used by: B-14
<a id="anthropic-code-execution-mcp"></a>
- **[Code execution with MCP: building more efficient agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/code-execution-with-mcp)**: Anthropic, Adam Jones, Conor Kelly, 2025
  Shows that loading many tool definitions and piping intermediate results through the model wastes context.
  - Tool definitions loaded upfront can mean hundreds of thousands of tokens before reading a request.
  - Intermediate results passing through the model repeatedly add large token costs.
  - Example workflow dropped from 150,000 to 2,000 tokens with code execution.
  - Used by: S-08
<a id="anthropic-advanced-tool-use"></a>
- **[Introducing advanced tool use on the Claude Developer Platform](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use)**: Anthropic, Bin Wu et al., 2025
  Quantifies MCP tool-definition overhead and introduces the Tool Search Tool.
  - "58 tools consuming approximately 55K tokens before the conversation even starts".
  - Per server: GitHub ~26K tokens for 35 tools; Slack ~21K for 11 tools.
  - Deferring definitions via tool search cut token use ~85% and improved tool-selection accuracy in their evals.
  - Used by: B-10, H-06, S-08
<a id="anthropic-agent-skills-post"></a>
- **[Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills)**: Anthropic, Barry Zhang, Keith Lazuka, Mahesh Murag, 2025
  Introduces Agent Skills and their progressive-disclosure loading model.
  - Only name and description are preloaded; they decide when a skill activates.
  - Full SKILL.md loads on relevance; bundled files load only as needed.
  - Used by: S-03, S-06
<a id="anthropic-long-running-harnesses"></a>
- **[Effective harnesses for long-running agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-harnesses-for-long-running-agents)**: Anthropic, Justin Young, 2025
  Describes progress files and git history so fresh context windows can pick up multi-session work.
  - "compaction isn't sufficient" on its own for multi-window builds.
  - A progress notes file plus git log lets a new session recover state quickly.
  - Used by: B-07, B-13, H-07, S-10

### Research papers

<a id="liu-lost-in-the-middle"></a>
- **[Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2307.03172)**: TACL / arXiv, Nelson F. Liu, Kevin Lin, John Hewitt, Ashwin Paranjape, Michele Bevilacqua, Fabio Petroni, Percy Liang, 2023
  Shows long-context models use information at the start and end of the input far better than in the middle.
  - Accuracy is U-shaped over position of the relevant information.
  - Performance drops significantly when the needed fact sits in the middle of a long context.
  - Used by: B-01
<a id="hsieh-ruler"></a>
- **[RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06654)**: arXiv, Cheng-Ping Hsieh, Simeng Sun, Samuel Kriman, Shantanu Acharya, Dima Rekesh, Fei Jia, Yang Zhang, Boris Ginsburg, 2024
  Synthetic benchmark showing effective context is often much shorter than advertised.
  - Of models claiming 32K+ contexts, only about half held satisfactory performance at 32K.
  - Degradation grows with length and task complexity beyond simple needle retrieval.
  - Used by: B-08
<a id="chroma-context-rot"></a>
- **[Context Rot: How Increasing Input Tokens Impacts LLM Performance](https://www.trychroma.com/research/context-rot)**: Chroma, Kelly Hong, Anton Troynikov, Jeff Huber, 2025
  Technical report on 18 LLMs showing reliability falls as input length grows, even on simple tasks.
  - Performance varies significantly with input length even on trivial tasks.
  - Even a single distractor lowers accuracy.
  - LongMemEval: focused ~300-token prompts beat full ~113k-token prompts by a wide margin.
  - Used by: B-08
<a id="modarressi-nolima"></a>
- **[NoLiMa: Long-Context Evaluation Beyond Literal Matching](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.05167)**: arXiv (ICML 2025), Ali Modarressi, Hanieh Deilamsalehy, Franck Dernoncourt, Trung Bui, Ryan A. Rossi, Seunghyun Yoon, Hinrich Schütze, 2025
  Needle tests without lexical overlap reveal steep long-context degradation.
  - At 32K, 11 models fell below 50% of their short-context baseline.
  - GPT-4o dropped from 99.3% to 69.7%.
  - Used by: B-08
<a id="du-context-length-hurts"></a>
- **[Context Length Alone Hurts LLM Performance Despite Perfect Retrieval](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.05381)**: arXiv, Yufeng Du, Minyang Tian, Srikanth Ronanki, et al., 2025
  Shows sheer input length degrades reasoning even when the relevant evidence is perfectly retrieved.
  - Performance fell 13.9%-85% with longer inputs across five models on math, QA and coding.
  - Having the model recite the evidence first partially mitigates the drop.
  - Used by: B-08
<a id="laban-lost-multi-turn"></a>
- **[LLMs Get Lost In Multi-Turn Conversation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.06120)**: arXiv, Philippe Laban, Hiroaki Hayashi, Yingbo Zhou, Jennifer Neville, 2025
  Multi-turn, underspecified conversations cause large and unrecoverable quality drops.
  - Average 39% performance drop across six tasks versus single-turn.
  - Models commit to early assumptions and rarely recover from a wrong turn.
  - Used by: B-13
<a id="lulla-agents-md-efficiency"></a>
- **[On the Impact of AGENTS.md Files on the Efficiency of AI Coding Agents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.20404)**: arXiv, Jai Lal Lulla, Seyedmoein Mohsenimofidi, Matthias Galster, Jie M. Zhang, Sebastian Baltes, Christoph Treude, 2026
  Paired with/without AGENTS.md runs of Codex on 124 PRs from 10 repositories.
  - With AGENTS.md: median runtime -28.64%, output tokens -16.58%, completion comparable.
  - Limits: one agent (Codex), small PRs (<=100 LOC, <=5 files), light correctness checks, output tokens only.
  - Used by: S-12
<a id="gloaguen-evaluating-agents-md"></a>
- **[Evaluating AGENTS.md: Are Repository-Level Context Files Helpful for Coding Agents?](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.11988)**: arXiv (ETH Zurich SRI Lab), Thibaud Gloaguen, Niels Mündler, Mark Müller, Veselin Raychev, Martin Vechev, 2026
  Across agents and models, context files did not generally raise success but raised inference cost.
  - Context files do "not generally improve task success rates" and raise inference cost by over 20%.
  - Agents follow context-file instructions well, so unnecessary requirements make tasks harder.
  - Repository overviews were ineffective; files help most for non-standard practices.
  - Used by: S-01, S-05, S-07, S-12
<a id="zhang-skill-defects"></a>
- **[What Keeps Agent Skills from Being Reusable? Evidence from 138K SKILL.md Files](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08453)**: arXiv, Chi Zhang, Yimin Liu, Xinze Chen, Ping Ji, 2026
  Large-scale audit of public SKILL.md files, dominated by routing-metadata defects.
  - 91.8% of skills have at least one defect; 67.0% have a routing (description) defect.
  - Missing trigger guidance (52.3%), overlong (14.3%) and non-functional (13.5%) descriptions are common.
  - In a BM25 routing test, clean-metadata skills hit@1 88.5% vs 82.6% for defective ones.
  - Used by: S-03
<a id="yang-swe-agent"></a>
- **[SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793)**: arXiv, John Yang, Carlos E. Jimenez, Alexander Wettig, Kilian Lieret, Shunyu Yao, Karthik Narasimhan, Ofir Press, 2024
  Shows interface design (concise, bounded tool output) materially changes coding-agent success.
  - Search returns at most 50 results; beyond that the agent is told to refine the query.
  - File viewer of 100 lines beat full-file display (18.0% vs 12.7% resolved) and 30 lines (14.3%).
  - Observations older than the last five are collapsed to a single line.
  - Used by: B-03, B-12, B-14, H-02
<a id="lindenbauer-complexity-trap"></a>
- **[The Complexity Trap: Simple Observation Masking Is as Efficient as LLM Summarization for Agent Context Management](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.21433)**: arXiv, Tobias Lindenbauer, Igor Slinko, Ludwig Felder, Egor Bogomolov, Yaroslav Zharov, 2025
  On SWE-bench Verified, masking old tool observations matches LLM summarisation at lower cost.
  - Observation masking roughly halves cost versus unmanaged context.
  - Solve rates equal or slightly better than LLM summarisation; a hybrid adds 7-11% efficiency.
  - Used by: B-12
<a id="zhang-ace-context-collapse"></a>
- **[Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.04618)**: arXiv, Qizheng Zhang et al., 2025
  Identifies brevity bias and context collapse when contexts are repeatedly rewritten or summarised.
  - Brevity bias: concise summaries drop domain insights.
  - Context collapse: iterative rewriting erodes details over time.
  - Used by: B-07
<a id="lumer-dont-break-cache"></a>
- **[Don't Break the Cache: An Evaluation of Prompt Caching for Long-Horizon Agentic Tasks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.06007)**: arXiv, Elias Lumer, Faheem Nizar, Akshaya Jangiti, Kevin Frank, Anmol Gulati, Mandar Phadate, Vamse Kumar Subbiah, 2026
  Measures prompt-caching savings for agents across OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.
  - Caching cut API cost 41-80% and time-to-first-token 13-31% over 500+ sessions.
  - Keeping dynamic content at the end and excluding dynamic tool results beats naive full-context caching.
  - Used by: B-09

### Practitioner writing

<a id="manus-context-engineering"></a>
- **[Context Engineering for AI Agents: Lessons from Building Manus](https://manus.im/blog/Context-Engineering-for-AI-Agents-Lessons-from-Building-Manus)**: Manus, Yichao 'Peak' Ji, 2025
  Production lessons on cache-friendly, append-only agent context.
  - "KV-cache hit rate is the single most important metric" for production agents.
  - Keep prefixes stable (no timestamps), append-only, and mask tools instead of removing them.
  - Compress restorably (keep the URL/path, drop the content); keep failed actions visible.
  - Used by: B-09, B-12, S-10
<a id="cognition-dont-build-multi-agents"></a>
- **[Don't Build Multi-Agents](https://cognition.com/blog/dont-build-multi-agents)**: Cognition, Walden Yan, 2025
  Argues context splitting across agents causes conflicting implicit decisions.
  - Share context and full agent traces, not just individual messages.
  - Actions carry implicit decisions; parallel agents without shared context make conflicting ones.
  - Suggests a dedicated model to compress history into key details and decisions.
  - Used by: B-06, B-15
<a id="langchain-context-engineering"></a>
- **[Context Engineering for Agents](https://www.langchain.com/blog/context-engineering-for-agents)**: LangChain, LangChain team, 2025
  Groups context techniques into write, select, compress and isolate.
  - Tool feedback accumulates across turns and can exceed or degrade the window.
  - Isolation (sub-agents) and compression are complementary levers.
  - Used by: B-12
<a id="breunig-how-contexts-fail"></a>
- **[How Long Contexts Fail](https://www.dbreunig.com/2025/06/22/how-contexts-fail-and-how-to-fix-them.html)**: dbreunig.com, Drew Breunig, 2025
  Names four long-context failure modes with cited examples.
  - Poisoning, distraction, confusion (superfluous tools/content) and clash (conflicting content).
  - Cites a Gemini agent past ~100k tokens repeating past actions instead of planning.
  - Cites evidence that adding tools degrades function-calling accuracy.
  - Used by: S-02, S-08
<a id="willison-context-engineering"></a>
- **[Context engineering](https://simonwillison.net/2025/Jun/27/context-engineering/)**: simonwillison.net, Simon Willison, 2025
  Records the adoption of 'context engineering', quoting Tobi Lutke and Andrej Karpathy.
  - Karpathy: the job is filling the window with just the right information.
  - Links Karpathy's original post (x.com/karpathy/status/1937902205765607626), not fetched directly.
<a id="mixon-dotagents"></a>
- **[dotagents-standard: an agent skill for the .agents layout](https://www.jeffmixon.com/post/dotagents-standard-agent-skill/)**: jeffmixon.com, Jeff Mixon, 2026
  Describes a slim AGENTS.md router plus a .agents/ directory loaded by progressive disclosure.
  - Keep the root instruction file a router; pull rules, context, specs on demand.
  - Separates standing rules from evolving memory and task specs.
  - Instruction files grow until nobody, human or model, reads them end to end.
  - Used by: S-06
<a id="aider-edit-formats"></a>
- **[Edit formats](https://aider.chat/docs/more/edit-formats.html)**: Aider
  Compares whole-file and diff edit formats for LLM code edits.
  - Whole-file edits are "slow and costly" because the model returns the entire file.
  - Diff formats return only changed parts.
  - Used by: B-17
